verdicts.claim: A 'welded shape' has no special type — it is an ordinary Primitive joined by the normal free-place auto-bond, which picks the nearest SAME-COLOUR primitive within AUTO_BOND_RADIUS, so a weld on your tower is always your own shape (controls.ts:1483).
verdicts.note: The mechanism is real but the report names ONE of TWO call sites and cites the filter at the wrong line. controls.ts:1483 is `const targetId = this.pickPrimitiveInRange(AUTO_BOND_RADIUS, targetRefPos);` — correct. But the same-colour filter it quotes lives at controls.ts:1732 (`if (myColor !== undefined && p.placerColor !== myColor) continue;`), inside `pickPrimitiveInRange` at :1724, not at 1483. The missed second site is the AUTHORITATIVE one: `pickHostTargetPrimitive` (placePrimitive.ts:610) — and it carries a filter the client path does not (placePrimitive.ts:620: `if (lockedPrims.has(p.id)) continue; // S107 P4 — exclude spawner-locked ring nodes from auto-bond`). See corrections: that filter decides WHO can create a weld. AUTO_BOND_RADIUS = 60 confirmed at constants.ts:824.

corrections: ⛔⛔ THE REPORT'S CENTRAL COST CLAIM IS BACKWARDS, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE RULING. It says the weld bond "contributes nothing to the tower's health". It contributes a great deal. `damageConnector` prices EVERY connector against the whole component: damage.ts:395-396 `const comp = componentOf(anchor, world.primitives, world.bonds);` / `const pool = structurePoolFifths(comp.bondIds.size);`, and its docblock at damage.ts:346-348 states it outright — "the pool is **STRUCTURE-WIDE**, not per-bond … `structurePoolFifths(n)` = `n × (5 + n)` … ALL damage standing anywhere on the structure counts toward the next connector", "derived live, never stored". A tier-3 race tower is 3 connectors (raceTowerIds.ts:28 `RACE_TOWER_SIZE = 3`) → pool 24. Weld ONE shape on → 4 connectors → pool 36. **One stray shape is a hidden +50 % durability buff on every connector of that tower, and it is invisible because it sits under the art.** healthBar.ts:242-243 says the same thing in its own words: "a POOL belongs to a connected component, not to a building … two towers welded into one lattice genuinely share one pool." This inverts owner_question #2 and #3: a weld is not clutter the player forgot to clean up, it is a cheap exploit-shaped buff. Option D stops being a tidy-up and becomes a balance change.

⛔ AND ONE SHAPE CAN MINT UP TO THREE BONDS, NOT ONE. constants.ts:875 `export const REDUNDANT_BOND_K = 3;`, and redundantBondTargets.ts:89 `if (selectedIds.length >= args.k - 1) break;` — so the primary auto-bond plus up to two redundancy bonds, all within AUTO_BOND_RADIUS (controls.ts:1785 `radius: AUTO_BOND_RADIUS`), all into the primary target's own component (placePrimitive.ts:334 `if (!mergedComponents.has(extraId))` refuses anything else). On a 3-ring whose nodes all sit inside 60 px, one hand-placed shape can take the component from 3 connectors to 6: pool 24 → 66, a 2.75× buff. The report models the weld as a single connector throughout — findings, fix options and owner questions alike.

⛔ WHO CAN REACH IT — the report names one call site; there are two and THEY DISAGREE. `collectSpawnerLockedPrimitiveIds` (placePrimitive.ts:677) locks the entire connected component of every live spawner's anchor, and both host helpers skip it (placePrimitive.ts:620 and :654, `if (lockedPrims.has(p.id)) continue; // S107 P4 — exclude spawner-locked ring nodes from auto-bond`). Its own docblock at :665-668 says why: "Auto-bond candidacy excludes these so the recipe's exact bond-degree … is never raised by an adjacent placement." ⚠ BUT THAT LOCK IS ONLY CONSULTED ON THE REMOTE-ORIGIN BRANCH — placePrimitive.ts:198 `if (isRemoteOrigin && action.placementPos !== undefined) {` and placeFromFree.ts:186-188, whose `else` arm takes `effectiveTargetId = action.targetPrimitiveId` straight from controls.ts's unfiltered `pickPrimitiveInRange` (:1724-1742, no lock test). ⇒ **A JOINER CANNOT WELD ONTO ANY LIVE TOWER. THE HOST AND THE SOLO PLAYER CAN.** The merge sweep is closed on both paths (placePrimitive.ts:390 `if (lockedPrims.has(candId)) continue; // … (covers the local path too)`), so the ONLY live vector is the local-origin 60 px primary auto-bond and its redundancy bonds. The report presents the weld as a universal mechanic; it is the local player's privilege, and that is the scope line owner_question #4 should be drawn on.

VOLTKIN IS THE THIRD COVER PUBLISHER AND THE REPORT NEVER ENUMERATES IT. towerCover.test.ts:270-272 names exactly three: `towerRenderer.ts` ('the twelve race towers + the six tier-9 boss towers'), `structureRampRenderer.ts` ('the five RAMP_SPECS towers, spawners AND defenders'), `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts` ('the Voltkin TV'), publishing at towerRenderer.ts:313, structureRampRenderer.ts:223, voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576. The report's fix_shape lists towerRenderer.ts:312 (it is 313) and never analyses the Voltkin chain as a topology. Its conclusion survives — voltkin.ts:292 `if (p.bonds.size !== expectedDegree) {` kills the chain on any weld, endpoint or middle — but the report's "five topologies" is its own number, not one the tree supports, and it reached the right answer without checking the third publisher.

THE STINK TOWER IS A BIGGER VERSION OF THE SAME COMPLAINT AND IS ABSENT FROM THE REPORT. towerCover.test.ts:286 pins `stinkTowerRenderer.ts` among the files asserted to contain ZERO `markTowerCover(` calls. It is a live star tower with art (stinkTower.ts:145 `isStarAt(world, squareId, STINK_HUB_TYPE, STINK_LEAF_TYPE, STINK_TOWER_HUB_DEGREE)`), so ALL of its shapes and connectors show through it, welded or not — and handoff next-step #2 is literally "Connector hiding for the STINK TOWER". A ruling scoped to welds alone leaves that tower's whole ring bright, which is the owner's same visual complaint with a bigger surface.

OPTION C IS GEOMETRICALLY UNDERSPECIFIED. `T3_TOWER_ART_PX` does not exist — towerFrames.ts:131 is `export const T3_TOWER_SPRITE_PX = 84;` (with `T9_TOWER_SPRITE_PX = 150` at :132), and towerFrames.ts:139 is `export const TOWER_SPRITE_ANCHOR = { x: 0.5, y: 1 } as const;` — FOOT-anchored, documented at :135-138 as deliberate. Meanwhile each RAMP_SPEC carries its own `spritePx` AND a separate `artPx` (structureRamp.ts:363-364 HUB_SPRITE_PX / HUB_ART_PX, and so on for all five), and voltkin uses `TV_ART_PX`. So "is this neighbour inside the sprite's drawn box" is three different box derivations against a bottom-centre anchor, not one 84 px square. That is the part of the estimate that is light.

A DETERMINISM NOTE ABOUT THE EXISTING CODE, NOT ONLY A FUTURE HELPER. structureRamp.ts:510-516's star branch iterates `anchor.bonds` — a Set, insertion order — pushing into the `members` and `bonds` ARRAYS. Everything it currently feeds is order-insensitive (centroid is a sum, `newestTick` a max, `bankedFifths` a sum, health reads `bonds.length`), so it is safe today. But a `coverExtrasOf` appended to those same arrays inherits that ordering, and any consumer that later reads `members[0]` or drives a per-index collapse sequence re-enters the S155 N1 class. The report warns about a new helper's ordering; it does not note the walk it would extend is already order-dependent in shape. `ringShape.ts` got this right on purpose (ascending-id `sameTypeNeighbours`) and says so.

VERIFIED SOUND, worth recording so nobody re-checks it: the feature is genuinely live (`beginTowerCoverFrame` called at main.ts:3981, so towerCover.ts:143's `let active = false;` default is not the S180 'archived subsystem' trap); `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 47` at protocol.ts:704, so the report's four_sites figure is current (project CLAUDE.md still says 46 — stale, and not this lane's scope); the raid-aims-blind reasoning is not the report's inference but an in-tree verified note at spawnerZoneRenderer.ts:137-142 — "the raid pick in `controls.ts` never consults `coverAlphaForBond`, so an invisible connector is still clickable and still raidable"; and the shared-leaf hazard behind Option B is real and documented at starShape.ts:53-71, including "A shared leaf is a shared weakness — eat one Circle and BOTH towers fall."
net_assessment: STRUCTURALLY SOUND, MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE — do not ship the owner questions as written. 11 of 17 findings CONFIRMED verbatim, 5 PARTIAL (four on citation drift, one on a dropped clause), 0 fully REFUTED. The probe got the hard part right: the weld is a real, live, open owner call (canon:388, and the feature IS active — beginTowerCoverFrame at main.ts:3981, which the probe never checked); it is not a z-order defect; the exclusion at towerRenderer.ts:79 is deliberate and stated; the pentagram/star-hub eliminations hold exactly; and the ring-branch observation (structureRamp.ts:518, the only 'ring' in RAMP_SPECS) is a genuinely sharp catch. The fix_shape's one hard constraint — widen COVER separately from the MEMBER WALK, because rampMembersAt feeds sprite, hit box, muzzle and health — is correct and well-evidenced. But three things are wrong enough to change the ruling the owner would give. (1) The probe tells him a weld's connector "contributes nothing to the tower's health"; damage.ts:396 prices every connector against `structurePoolFifths(comp.bondIds.size)` over the whole component, so one weld takes a 3-ring from pool 24 to 36 (+50 %), and with REDUNDANT_BOND_K = 3 one shape can mint three bonds and reach 66 (2.75×) — a hidden buff, not clutter. (2) It presents the weld as universally reachable; S107 P4's spawner lock is wired only into the remote-origin branch, so a JOINER cannot weld onto any live tower while the host and the solo player can — that asymmetry is the real scope line for question #4. (3) R136 permits a FOREIGN-type weld only; a same-type stray still un-makes the race tower (ringShape.ts:36), and the summary and questions drop that. Also missing: the Voltkin chain as the third cover publisher, and the stink tower, which publishes no cover at all and is the same complaint at a larger size. GRADING THE ESTIMATES — size_estimate: Micro for the probe is FAIR; B/E at Micro-to-Standard FAIR; C is UNDERSTATED (three publishers, three box derivations, a foot anchor at towerFrames.ts:139, plus the shared-leaf case) — call it Standard; D is understated in kind, because correction #1 makes it a balance change with damage-suite fallout, not only a placement-legality change. four_sites_risk: the renderer-only verdict is CORRECT and properly evidenced (towerCover.ts:10-15, PROTOCOL_VERSION 47), and its two shortcut hazards are the right two — but it is incomplete, because the weld ALREADY moves a sim number today, so "no sim impact" is true of the fix and false of the thing being ruled on. tests_owed is the strongest section and should be kept, with one addition: a behavioural test pinning `structurePoolFifths(comp.bondIds.size)` before and after a weld, so whichever way he rules, the durability side of it cannot drift unpinned the way this one did.
